title: Operational Excellence pillar (run and observe systems)
hook: Operational Excellence means running workloads reliably through automation, observability, and safe change. You learn from operations and feed improvements back into design.

blocks.text: Design principles: perform operations as code, annotate documentation, make frequent small reversible changes, refine procedures from events, and anticipate failure. Key practices include Infrastructure as Code (IaC), CI/CD pipelines, runbooks, Game Days, and blameless postmortems.

entries.plainDefinition: Templates define infra — CloudFormation, CDK, Terraform

blocks.text: Interviewers ask how you deploy without downtime and how you know a service is healthy before customers complain. Operational Excellence separates teams that firefight from teams with automated rollback and SLO-driven alerts.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: ops as code, small changes, observability, runbooks, learn from incidents.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Automate deployments
items.body: CI/CD with staged rollouts, health checks, and automatic rollback.

items.title: Instrument observability
items.body: Metrics, logs, traces with dashboards and SLO-based alarms.

items.title: Document operations
items.body: Runbooks linked to alarms; architecture diagrams kept current.

items.title: Improve from events
items.body: Postmortems produce action items tracked to completion.

diagram.title: Ops flywheel
diagram.source:
flowchart TB
  DEPLOY[Automated deploy] --> OBS[Observe metrics/logs]
  OBS --> ALARM[Alarm fires]
  ALARM --> RUNBOOK[Runbook response]
  RUNBOOK --> POST[Postmortem]
  POST --> DEPLOY

snippet.label: CodePipeline deploy stage
snippet.code:
DeployStage:
  Actions:
    - Name: ECSDeploy
      ActionTypeId:
        Category: Deploy
        Provider: ECS
      Configuration:
        ClusterName: prod
        ServiceName: api
        FileName: imagedefinitions.json
snippet.explanation: Automated deploy — core Operational Excellence practice.

snippet.label: CloudWatch alarm on error rate
snippet.code:
Api5xxAlarm:
  Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
  Properties:
    MetricName: HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count
    Threshold: 10
    EvaluationPeriods: 2
    AlarmActions:
      - !Ref PagerDutyTopic

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Manual console changes not in IaC. Alarms with no runbook link. Postmortems without tracked action items.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: deployment frequency and MTTR dashboards; percentage of infra under IaC; alarm coverage ratio (alarms with runbooks / total critical metrics).

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying "we have CloudWatch" without SLOs, runbooks, or rollback — rejected. Strong answer: automated deploy, observable SLOs, learned postmortems.

interviewTakeaways: Operational Excellence = automate ops, observe, small reversible changes, learn from failure.
Manual console changes violate ops-as-code principle.
Wire alarms to runbooks and track postmortem actions in Jira.
60s: IaC, CI/CD, observability, runbooks, postmortems. Measure deploy frequency and MTTR. Game Days prove readiness.
Follow-up: how do you roll back a bad ECS deployment?
commonPitfalls: No rollback plan — rejected when interviewer asks about failed deploy.
Strong answer: blue/green or rolling with health checks and automatic rollback.
